wizard.pageHeaderDescription: Let's get your Discord bot up and running — follow the steps below

step0.heading: Create a Discord Application
step0.description: First, you need to create an application on Discord's Developer Portal. This only takes a minute.
step0.step1Desc: Click the button below to open it in a new tab.
step0.step2Desc: It's in the top-right corner. Name it anything you like (e.g. "PZ Server Bot").
step0.step3Desc: In the left sidebar of your new application, click <1>Bot</1>. Discord may auto-create a bot user, or you may see an "Add Bot" button — click it if so.
step0.whyBotTitle: Why do I need a bot?
step0.whyBotDesc: A Discord bot lets your panel send messages, register slash commands, and bridge in-game chat to a Discord channel. It runs through this panel, so you do not need separate hosting.

step1.heading: Copy Your Bot Token
step1.description: On the Bot page in the Developer Portal, click <1>"Reset Token"</1> (or "Copy" if visible), then paste it below.
step1.warningDesc: Discord only shows the token once after you reset it. If you lose it, you will need to generate a new one. Treat it like a password and never share it publicly.

step2.heading: Enable Privileged Intents
step2.description: Still on the <1>Bot</1> page in the Developer Portal, scroll down to <2>"Privileged Gateway Intents"</2> and enable these:
step2.serverMembersIntentWhy: Required to check user roles for admin commands
step2.messageContentIntentWhy: Required for two-way chat bridge (Discord ↔ Game)
step2.saveReminderDesc: After toggling the intents on, scroll down and click the Save Changes button on the Discord page.

step3.heading: Invite the Bot to Your Discord Server
step3.descriptionWithInvite: Click the button below to invite your bot. Select your Discord server from the dropdown, then click "Authorize".
step3.descriptionNoInvite: We need your bot token to generate an invite link. Go back to Step 2 and paste + verify your token first, or use the manual method below.
step3.permissionsIncludedList: Send Messages, Embed Links, Read Message History, Use Slash Commands
step3.permissionsIncludedHelp: Send Messages and Embed Links let the bot post status updates and command replies. Read Message History is required by Discord for reliable message replies. None of these permissions let the bot manage your server, roles, or channels.
step3.manualInviteIntro: If you have not verified your token yet, you can still invite the bot manually.
step3.manualStep1: In the Developer Portal, go to your app → <1>OAuth2</1> → <2>URL Generator</2>
step3.manualStep3: Under "Bot Permissions", check <1>Send Messages</1>, <2>Embed Links</2>, <3>Read Message History</3>, <4>Use Slash Commands</4>
step3.manualStep4: Copy the generated URL at the bottom and open it in your browser
step3.manualStep5: Select your Discord server and click <1>Authorize</1>
step3.tip: Tip: go back to Step 2 and verify your token — we'll generate the invite link automatically.

step4.heading: Configure Server IDs
step4.description: The bot needs your Discord server's ID to register slash commands. You can also set a notification channel and an admin role.
step4.devModeCopyIdHint: Now you can right-click servers, channels, and roles to see a <1>"Copy ID"</1> option.
step4.guildIdHelp: Right-click your Discord server name → <1>Copy Server ID</1>
step4.guildIdError: Invalid format — should be a 17-19 digit number
step4.channelIdHelp: Right-click a text channel → <1>Copy Channel ID</1>. Used for notifications and two-way chat bridge.
step4.channelIdError: Invalid format — should be a 17-19 digit number
step4.adminRoleHelp: Right-click a role → <1>Copy Role ID</1>. Only Discord members with this role can use bot commands — a separate role from this panel's own Roles & Permissions. Leave blank to allow everyone.
step4.adminRoleError: Invalid format — should be a 17-19 digit number

step5.heading: Ready to Launch!
step5.description: Review your configuration below, then save and start the bot.
step5.autoStartDesc: Automatically start the Discord bot when the panel launches

whatItDoes.title: What does the bot do?
whatItDoes.slashCommandsDesc: Control your PZ server from Discord with /status, /players, /start, /stop, /restart, /broadcast, /kick, and /rcon.
whatItDoes.chatBridgeDesc: Keep Discord and in-game chat in the same loop without switching tools during live admin work.
whatItDoes.eventNotifDesc: Send join/leave, start/stop, restart, death, and backup events straight to the channel your admins already watch.

management.pageHeaderDescription: Manage your Discord bot, slash commands, and event notifications

botStatus.title: Bot Status
botStatus.dependencyNote: Notifications, slash commands, and the chat bridge all depend on the bot staying connected to the configured channel.

gatewayIssue.label: Discord connection has been unstable for a while — alerts and commands may be delayed until it recovers.

channelOutsideGuild.title: Some notifications aren't being sent
channelOutsideGuild.body: Channel {{channels}} isn't in the server set as the Guild (Server) ID, so the bot no longer posts there. Pick a channel from that server, or set the Guild ID to the channel's server.

commandPermissions.title: Command Permissions
commandPermissions.description: Control who can use each slash command. Assign a permission tier per command.
commandPermissions.independenceTitle: Not the same roles as this panel
commandPermissions.independenceDesc: Admin and Moderator here are Discord roles, set via the Admin/Moderator Role ID fields below — separate from this panel's own Roles & Permissions. A Discord account is not linked to any panel account, so a user's panel role has no effect on what they can run here, and holding a Discord Admin/Moderator role grants nothing inside the panel.
commandPermissions.savedMessage: Command permissions saved. Slash commands re-registered.

configuration.title: Bot Configuration
configuration.guildIdError: Invalid format — use a 17-19 digit server ID
configuration.channelIdError: Invalid format — use a 17-19 digit channel ID
configuration.adminRoleHelp: Full access for role-protected commands. Server owners and Discord Administrators always retain access. This is a Discord role, independent of this panel's Roles & Permissions.
configuration.adminRoleError: Invalid format — use a 17-19 digit role ID
configuration.modRoleHelp: Can use "moderator" tier commands. Without a configured role, role-protected commands remain locked. This is a Discord role, independent of this panel's Roles & Permissions.
configuration.modRoleError: Invalid format — use a 17-19 digit role ID
configuration.autoStartDesc: The bot will start automatically when the panel boots up
configuration.chatRelayDesc: Bridge chat both ways between the game server and Discord
configuration.scopeOptionPublic: All public chat (General, Say, Local, Shout)
configuration.scopeHelp: Faction, safehouse, radio and admin chat are never forwarded. Build 42 records ordinary talking as Say, so "General tab only" relays very little.
configuration.scopeWarningPublic: Local chat is forwarded to Discord. Choose General tab only to keep player proximity chat private.
configuration.relayChannelPlaceholder: Leave empty to use main channel
configuration.relayChannelHelp: Relay game chat and Discord messages through a separate channel. Leave empty to use the main channel above.
configuration.relayChannelError: Invalid format — use a 17-19 digit channel ID
configuration.wipeNote: Moving the bot to a new Discord server? Use wipe to remove the stored Discord setup and restart the wizard cleanly.

toasts.wipeConfirmDesc: This clears the saved bot token, guild and channel IDs, role IDs, chat relay channel and Discord event notification setup, and puts each command's permission tier back to its default. A command that needs a permission you don't hold in this panel keeps its current tier. Auto-start and the chat relay go back to their defaults, which are on: once a new token is set up, the bot starts with the panel and relays all public chat both ways through the notification channel. The bot will stop and the page will return to first-time setup.
toasts.wipeSuccess: Discord bot settings wiped. You can start setup from scratch.
toasts.wipeSuccessKeptTiers: Discord bot settings wiped. These commands kept their permission tier because they need permissions you don't hold in this panel: {{commands}}

capabilityGate.connection: Only someone who holds every permission the bot's commands need can change this: the owner of the bot's Discord server and anyone with its admin role can run every command.
capabilityGate.modRole: Only someone who holds the permissions the Moderator-tier commands need can change this: anyone with this role can run those commands.
